title: A template inferred from the argument carries the argument type back to the caller

ground_truth.statement: identity() is declared as @template T / @param T $value / @return T. The call identity(5) therefore has both the value 5 and the type int, and under declare(strict_types=1) an int is not accepted for strlen()'s string parameter. strlen(identity(5)) is unreachable and throws; strlen(identity('abc')) is the control that runs and returns 3.

notes: A green row kept as a regression guard: all three analyzers resolve T from the argument and report that the int reaches strlen. The forbidden predicate on line 26 is the asymmetric control - the same generic call with a string argument must stay silent, so a tool cannot pass by reporting argument errors unconditionally. The runtime script proves the value identity (identity(5) is 5) and the strict-mode consequence (strlen(identity(5)) throws a TypeError) rather than relying on a tool's inference. The template identity pattern is the one PHPStan's own fixture documents in tests/PHPStan/Analyser/nsrt/generics.php (line 13-15 of that file, pinned commit in provenance); this fixture is not a copy of it.

sources.note: documents the @template T / @param T / @return T identity pattern; fixture rewritten
